question: Do Democrats win control of the US Senate in the 2026 elections
quote: But I think it's just such a 50-50. I'm going to say Democrats right now have the advantage. So 51%. But it's so close in all these states that it's too hard to render a verdict.
turn_text: Oh man, what a terrible question, Rich. I go back and forth with this. It depends on my mood. My mood this morning is kind of optimistic. Sometimes I'm not optimistic. And it's such a toss-up that I think both of those interpretations fit. But I really see a lot of softness for Democrats in Maine and Michigan. And if I saw a single poll that had Mike Rogers on top, right now it's a 1.2 point race depending on the poll you look at. And Mike Rogers has not led in any major polls. So I'm inclined to say that it's El-Sayed's race to lose. But Rogers has momentum. El-Sayed doesn't. The conventional wisdom seems to be that Collins is in a better position than she was six years ago at least. If they lose one or both of those houses, they have no pathway really to the Senate majority because I don't think Iowa is going to flip necessarily. Texas and Alaska, Ohio and North Carolina are possible as a pathway even if Republicans manage to do better in the upper Midwest and Maine. But I think it's just such a 50-50. I'm going to say Democrats right now have the advantage. So 51%. But it's so close in all these states that it's too hard to render a verdict.
host_quote: So Noah Rothman, X question to you. Percentage odds that Democrats take the Senate at this very moment.
resolution_criteria: Which party controls the US Senate after the 2026 elections, including any runoffs: Democrats if they and the independents who caucus with them hold at least 51 seats, or 50 with a Democratic vice-presidential tiebreak; otherwise Republicans. A YES answer means Democrats. Decided by the Associated Press's call. If AP has not called it within 60 days of election day, the certified official result decides. Resolves when control is called.
outcome_source_title: AP: Democrats took the Senate late Tuesday (control call explainer)
